method: the first strange sheet: admitted locations across the whole mode roster, apportioned by a seeded draw
why: a correction sheet: the incumbent's tier was prefilled and the page ordered by its score

method: the unserved mode-and-location pairs of the same population, with the busy modes deliberately over-drawn at high score
why: anchored, and non-representative on purpose — it is aimed at where the incumbent was suspected of being wrong, so no rate on it is a base rate

method: locations carrying a top human tier, rendered through the rare hue families the pool draw under-serves
why: anchored, and drawn against the palette distribution rather than from it; location quality is conditioned on by a human before the page exists

method: the blind sheet's draw rule re-run — flat mode apportionment, pool palette, no head in the selection — and then served anchored
why: THE DRAW IS UNCONDITIONED AND THE PAGE IS NOT, and the second half is what decides: the incumbent's tier is prefilled and orders the page, so its labels are ceilings and it may never join the blind sheet

method: fresh location-and-mode pairs no prior sheet served, pool palette, served blind in a seeded shuffle
why: THE INSTRUMENT. Every other strange batch is a correction sheet served with the incumbent's own verdict, so this is the only unanchored reading of this population that exists

method: the threads mode over admitted locations — the location head's own stock above the good floor — apportioned evenly across the partitions by a seeded draw, one render per location at label fidelity, the map picked by the palette head out of a seeded neighbourhood of the shipped pool
why: A NEW GENERATION TYPE. threads is a niche mode no draw has ever served, so this head has never seen one and its scores on them are uninformed. The draw is unconditioned on any render-head score, but the locations are the location head's admitted stock, and the page prefills this head's own tier and orders the rows by its score, so a rate read on these labels measures agreement with that head and is not a base rate. The correction rate is what the batch was bought for.

method: the itinerary mode over an INDEPENDENT draw of the same shape as threads_promotion's — admitted locations apportioned evenly across the partitions, one render per location at label fidelity, palette-head pick — drawn separately and sharing zero locations with it, with the address opening at z1 wherever the pixel is z0, which is the production behavior
why: A NEW GENERATION TYPE, and the second half of one promotion question. Same standing as threads_promotion: uninformed head scores on an unseen mode, an admitted-stock draw, and the page prefills this head's own tier and orders the rows by its score, so a rate read on these labels measures agreement with that head and is not a base rate.

method: strange renders over run2-era material reached through the two channels new in that harvest — the twin channel and the plane-seed channel — drawn from an over-rendered pool weighted toward this head's own release bar, plus the one row out of run8h that a review flagged by name
why: bought to restate the acting strange release bar from labels rather than from a review verdict. The selection is weighted by this head's own P(>=3) toward 0.50, so it is conditioned on the head at selection as well as on the page, and it is non-representative on purpose: it is aimed at the band where the keep decision is actually close.

method: manufactured. One row per location, no location twice. Locations are places a person scored 3 or 4 on the location scale, extended into the highest-scoring admitted supply where a swatch quota could not be filled from those; every row stamps which tier it came from. Each location is aimed at one of the thin swatches `curate expressed` names, tried through maps the `curate coverage` panel says can reach it — here the maps of the `rare-colors-2026-08` drop — in modes drawn the way a production run draws them, under the identity palette recipe production uses. Every attempt was built and censused; what filled a quota is the share measured on the picture served, and every served row also cleared the render judge at >= 2 on that same picture.
why: A correction rate off these sheets is a CEILING and never a base rate: the population is enriched twice over, by location quality and by a passing score. Registered before the first pixel because the honest answer to `was a model score in the selection` is only available while the population is being drawn.

method: the contrast arm of the same manufacture, drawn identically in every respect but one: its maps are the ones the library already held before the `rare-colors-2026-08` drop, forced to the same target swatches. Its own batch so that a verdict about the colour and a verdict about the drop are separable from the store alone.
why: A correction rate off these sheets is a CEILING and never a base rate: the population is enriched twice over, by location quality and by a passing score. Registered before the first pixel because the honest answer to `was a model score in the selection` is only available while the population is being drawn.

method: a seeded stratified draw over the candidate ledger, banded on the SHIPPED render judge (artifact e62e8dba, floors.SCORING_HEAD) P(>=4) read at 640x360 ss2. Three bands — [0.85,0.95) [0.75,0.85) [0.60,0.75) — crossed with three strata assigned exclusively, colour first: mode `smooth`; candidates dominant (palettes.dominance) in dark_vivid_green, lime, teal or cyan; composite-kind modes. Smooth and strange kinds are drawn as separate batches into separate stores and are never pooled. Seed 20260826, one row per location, and up to two per location in the colour cells only, flagged per row in artifacts/curation/calibration/draw.jsonl. Already-labelled renders, person-rejected rows and pinned eval locations were excluded before the draw. The page is ordered by the judge and prefills its decode.
why: NO RATE COMPUTED OFF THESE ROWS IS AN EVAL RATE. The draw is banded on the incumbent judge and the page is anchored, so these rows measure agreement with the incumbent and any accuracy quoted from them is a ceiling. Fitting the P(>=4) crossover against them is the legitimate use; a quoted accuracy is not.

method: top of each of nine under-represented render modes by the shipped render judge's P(>=4) at 640x360 ss2, taken over the whole candidate ledger, unfiltered and unstratified; one row per (location, mode), ~33 a mode; excluded a recipe a finished store already holds a verdict on, a candidate a person rejected, and anything on a pinned evaluation location; served at 1280x720 ss2 through each row's own recipe with the autolevel operator replayed at that geometry
why: The draw IS the judge's own top, so no rate computed off these rows is an eval rate and any accuracy quoted from them is a ceiling. The rows exist because these nine modes are the ones the render judge has seen least and everything the pipeline believes about them comes from that judge; they are the evidence for a retrain that can rank these populations, and they cannot measure the incumbent.

method: Two blocks over the candidate ledger, cut and served as one page per store. (1) The 150 seats of the p2b_n150 program: curate seat --n 150 walking the clearing pool strongest-first under five selection rules (one per location, palette group cap, cell allowance, family allowance, twin) after a neutral pre-selection at radius 0.02, with mode floors at floor(n/100)=1. (2) 50 control rows drawn strongest-first by the shipped judge's P(>=4), one per location, over locations no seat holds, under no selection rule at all. Both blocks re-rendered fresh at 1280x720 ss2 and re-scored there; the 640x360 ss2 reading each row was selected on travels beside it.
why: An instrument for two unmeasured claims. Hard optimization against a learned score preferentially selects that score's false positives and nothing in this project reads them; and the seated floor is a learned proxy on bars set by volume-matching, never crossed against eyes, so a floor number today compares two solves and means nothing absolute. Pinned because a population selected BY the head is spent as an instrument the moment it trains one.

method: head-top per mode by the fitted rank key, over the nine sparsest modes by tier>=3 label count, after a mining leg aimed at those modes; at most two rows per (location, mode); rendered fresh at 1280x720 ss2
why: the objective was q3/q4 labels in modes that have almost none, so the draw is deliberately best-of rather than flat: a flat stratum spends the sitting on shapes already known. Model-driven selection and an anchored page, so train-side forever and never an instrument. Rates read off it are ceilings, not base rates.

method: direct_trap_multiply drawn under four mode-param variants (opacity 0.4, opacity 0.6, threshold 0.2, both) over the 77 places holding a clearing shipped-mode row plus an aimed breadth draw of never-opened admitted places; screened at P(>=3) >= 0.50 on the candidate column, one card per location, the location's best clearing row
why: the shipped direct_trap_multiply whitewashes: Blend::Multiply from white loses almost nothing perceptually per hit, and the render judge rewards that (Spearman(chroma, P(>=4)) = -0.269). The judge cannot settle whether the tinted variants are better, so Matt's eye decides. Screened on P(>=3) and NOT P(>=4) for the same reason.

method: One candidate-ledger row per LOCATION on the phoenix and phoenix:classic partitions — the location's best row by the shipped render judge's P(>=4) at 640x360ss2 — with every location already carrying a row in either finished store excluded, then the 100 locations immediately above and the 100 immediately below P(>=4)=0.5, so the page straddles the judge's own q3/q4 crossing rather than running from its top.
why: Cut to find phoenix locations the judge holds at q3 that are really q4. The band is centred on the judge's own 0.5 crossing, so every rate read off it is conditional on the judge having put the place near its boundary — it is not a base rate about the phoenix planes.

method: Three slices over the merged candidate pool, one candidate-ledger row per LOCATION and no location in two slices, every reading the shipped render judge's P(>=4) at 640x360ss2 and every location's row its own best by that score. S1: 120 smooth-routed locations in the judge's uncertainty band P(>=4) in [0.40,0.95), top 120 by score. S2: 120 locations in the same band over every strange-kind mode but direct_trap_multiply, split as evenly as the modes' band populations allow. S3: 60 bar-clearing locations (P(>=4) >= 0.50) whose dominant colour cell is below its allowance of 84 on the solve/empty_modes_n2000 record taken 2026-09-02T16:41:50Z, mode-balanced. Excluded before the draw: the phoenix and phoenix:classic partitions, every direct_trap_multiply row, every location already carrying a row in either finished store, and every place in pins.every_pinned. Cut as two sheets by store and routed by finished.routes_to on the join each card renders; each card carries its slice in section, facts and selected_on, and is re-scored at 1280x720 ss2 so both readings travel.
why: Training rows for the render judge's v6 retrain, drawn from three places the incumbent is known to mis-order: smooth's top end, the 3-vs-4 band across the roster, and rare colours. NOT an eval instrument and registered as such. The draw is banded on the incumbent's own score and the page prefills its decode and orders by it, so every rate read off these rows measures agreement with the incumbent and is a ceiling rather than a base rate. Train-side forever.

method: one card per LOCATION mined by the pc20m depth leg on phoenix:classic (width 3, full 11-mode roster, seed 20260903): the location's best candidate by the render judge's P(>=4) at 640x360ss2, re-rendered fresh at 1280x720ss2 and routed by finished.routes_to on the built join
why: Score-CONDITIONED twice over: the leg's ranked arm draws places on the location head's rank within partition, and the card at each place is the argmax over that place's candidates on the render judge. Anchored as well - the page serves the judge's own decode prefilled and reads good-to-bad by it. Train-side on both counts. Read no per-mode rate off it: the row at a place is that place's best mode, not a draw over modes.
